tagline: Red cliffs, the Virgin River and canyon trails
airports: St. George (SGU) is closest; Las Vegas (LAS) has the most flights

bestTime.text: Mild weather and the shuttle running daily. The Narrows can close when spring snowmelt runs high.
Very hot afternoons and flash-flood season. Hike early and carry water.
Pleasant temperatures and fall color along the river. The shuttle runs through late November.
Quiet and cool. With no shuttle on many winter days you can drive the canyon road.

tips: In shuttle season you cannot drive Zion Canyon Scenic Drive. Ride the free shuttle; no ticket is needed.
Angels Landing needs a permit from the lottery. You can hike to Scout Lookout without one.
The Narrows closes when the river runs above 150 cubic feet per second or during a flash flood warning.
Large vehicles are barred from the Zion to Mount Carmel highway and tunnel since June 7, 2026.
Hidden Canyon is closed and the East Rim Trail is partly closed after a rockfall near Weeping Rock.

temple.name: Temple of Sinawava and Riverside Walk

itineraries.title: Three days in Zion
itineraries.summary: Get oriented on the canyon floor on day one, walk into the Narrows and up to Scout Lookout on day two, and drive the east side through the tunnel on day three.
itineraries.season: The canyon shuttle runs daily from about March through late November; in 2026 there is no service from Nov. 29 to Dec. 25, when you can drive the canyon road. Day two depends on river flow and, for the chains, a permit.

plan.label: Day 1
plan.subtitle: Orientation, an easy river trail and the patriarchs

stops.text: Check in and park in Springdale or at the visitor center. Lots inside the park fill early.
Pick up a map and check river and trail conditions before you plan day two.
Walk the paved Pa'rus Trail along the Virgin River. It is the one Zion trail open to leashed pets and bikes.
Ride the shuttle to the Court of the Patriarchs viewpoint, then stop at Canyon Junction for evening light on the cliffs.
stops.status: Shuttle season: no private cars on the canyon road
stops.swap: On days with no shuttle service, drive the canyon road and park at the viewpoint pullouts.

plan.label: Day 2
plan.subtitle: The Riverside Walk, the Narrows and Scout Lookout

stops.text: Take the first shuttle to the Temple of Sinawava and walk the easy Riverside Walk to where the trail meets the river.
If conditions allow, wade upstream into the Narrows as far as you are comfortable and turn back well before you tire.
stops.status: Closes above 150 cubic feet per second or during a flash flood warning

stops.text: From the Grotto, climb the West Rim Trail to Scout Lookout. Continuing onto the Angels Landing chains needs a lottery permit.
stops.status: Scout Lookout: no permit. Angels Landing: permit required.

stops.text: Rest on the lawn at Zion Lodge before the shuttle back to Springdale.

plan.label: Day 3
plan.subtitle: The tunnel, Canyon Overlook and the slickrock country

stops.text: Drive the switchbacks of the Zion to Mount Carmel highway and through the tunnel. Large vehicles are not allowed on this road.
stops.status: Open, closes for snow, ice or rockfall

stops.text: Hike the short Canyon Overlook Trail just past the tunnel. Parking is very limited, so go early and be ready to circle back.
Continue to the cross-hatched sandstone of Checkerboard Mesa near the East Entrance, then head home.
